data.description:
## Discovered from

rebar-debug on bug `itchy-arbored-peccary` (3907-0110-7688-43bd), while verifying a handed-in
claim that the janitor had no caller. It has one — but exactly one.

## Problem

`start_background_janitor` has a single production invocation: the review-bot's FastAPI
lifespan, `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:134-136` (documented at
`infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:500-501`). Confirmed by both a plain `grep` for the name as a
string and a semantic `find_referencing_symbols`; the two agree.

So the janitor — the ONLY thing that reclaims `$REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR/rebar-gate-snapshots` — runs
only inside the long-lived review-bot server process. Every other host that resolves an attested
gate runs no janitor at all:

- a developer laptop running `rebar review-plan` / `review-code` / `verify-completion`
- a CI runner invoking the same gates
- any embedding of the library that is not the review-bot FastAPI app

On those hosts the store is append-only for the life of the machine. Measured on one developer
host (read-only inspection, nothing deleted):

| | |
|---|---|
| entries in the store | 64,021 |
| of which `tickets-<sha>` | 34,851 |
| size of a recent `tickets-<sha>` | ~861 MiB |
| `bytes.total` reports | 47.24 GiB |

Nothing has ever reclaimed any of it.

## Why this is separate from 3907

3907 fixes the *policy*: it implements the ADR-promised byte-total cap and makes the tickets
entries byte-accounted, so a size trigger exists and reads a true total. That is necessary but
it only helps where a janitor pass actually runs. This ticket is about the *cadence* — there is
no pass to apply the policy on any non-review-bot host.

## Constraint

ADR 0005 D5 is explicit that the janitor is "off the hot path ... never invoked from
populate/read", so a naive GC call inside `cache.acquire` would contradict the recorded
architecture and put an `flock` + full `iterdir` on every gate resolution. A design is needed,
not a one-liner. Sketches worth evaluating:

- an **operation-linked opportunistic pass** that is off the *critical* path — e.g. after a gate
  RESOLVES (not during populate), rate-limited by a stamp file so at most one pass runs per
  `interval_seconds` per host, and skipped entirely if the gc `flock` is contended
- a `rebar snapshot-gc` **CLI verb** an operator or a CI step can call explicitly, plus
  documentation of it in `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`
- starting the background thread from any long-lived rebar process, not just the review-bot app

The portability criterion (`project.portability`) rules out a fix whose only trigger is a
specific CI system; an operation-linked or in-process trigger is required.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A host that runs attested gates WITHOUT the review-bot server reclaims its snapshot store.
- [ ] The chosen trigger does not put GC work on the populate/read hot path (ADR 0005 D5 holds,
      or the ADR is amended with the reasoning).
- [ ] The trigger is operation-linked or in-process — not dependent on any one CI provider.
- [ ] A test observes reclamation happening on a simulated non-review-bot host RED before /
      GREEN after.
- [ ] `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` documents when a pass runs and how an operator forces one.
data.title: Snapshot janitor runs only in the review-bot process; every other host's store is append-only
